svg.title: Royalty, Insurance, and Share Recovery Architecture
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-specialty-asset-architecture; chapter number: 11; title: Royalty, Insurance, and Share Recovery Architecture; subtitle: One claimant working four custodian channels; chart type: org_architecture; center: role: Claimant or Heir; headcount: Every heir named in the will or letter of administration; focus: Name-variant searches across every state, portal, and registrar, backed by ID and probate or heirship proof.; spokes: role: Texas Comptroller; type: State custodian for royalties; kpi: MI02 royalties abandoned after 3 years; finder fee capped at 10%; $10,000 affidavit-of-heirship ceiling.; role: Well Operator; type: Royalty holder; kpi: Redirect future checks after the claim; claiming suspended royalties can cure title and restore pay status.; role: Policy Locator; type: Insurance search; kpi: Run NAIC and MissingMoney.com first; MIB costs $75 for policies after 1995 as an absolute last resort.; role: Share Registrar; type: Statutory dividend custodian; kpi: 7 years to the IEPFA in India, 6 years to the Nigerian trust fund; get the amount from the registrar, not the broker.; caption: Specialty assets escheat on the same dormancy mechanic, but each custodian channel has its own proof and fee rules.; assumptions note: Spokes group the custodians named by practitioners; dormancy periods and fees are as stated for Texas, India, and Nigeria only.; note: Attributed to Royalty Clerk; txcomptroller; Blue Mesa Minerals; Garden Shop Pro; Mint; Broadstreet Radio.
